subject: Re: Performance SLO benchmark methodology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@edgefin.com>
Cc: rafael.mendes@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO benchmark methodology

Hi Alice - great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call with the SRE and platform teams:

Summary of agreed SLO targets (please confirm these are what you expect us to validate):
- Latency: p95 generation latency < 300 ms for 512-token responses (non-streaming).
- Streaming: initial token latency < 50 ms and stable chunking every ~40-60 ms for continuous streaming scenarios.
- Throughput: sustained system throughput target ~200 req/s at 50 concurrent connections.
- Concurrency: support 50 concurrent user sessions with KV-cache warmup within first 2 minutes.
- Cold-start: model container cold-start time < 2s for warm VM images (no model download).

Benchmark methodology we propose to exchange and run:
- Prompt sets: we attached prompt_set_edgefin_v1.jsonl (representative production prompts + corner cases).
- Eval harness: redwood_eval_harness_v2.zip includes the runner, load profile configs, and exact measurement hooks (timestamps for first token, each chunk, and end-of-stream).
- Measurement defs: measurement_definitions.pdf defines p50/p95/p99, tail percentiles, and how we calculate streaming jitter. Reproducibility notes included.

Options for running the benchmark (pick one):
1) Redwood-run in your staging account: Redwood ops will run the harness in your staging project/region. Requires a temporary staging API key and access to a staging endpoint.
2) EdgeFin-run (self-run): we provide the harness and exact commands + a reproducibility checklist; you run it and share results and logs.

Attachments: prompt_set_edgefin_v1.jsonl, redwood_eval_harness_v2.zip, measurement_definitions.pdf, sample_run_results.csv

Next steps / asks:
- Confirm the SLO numbers above (latency/throughput/concurrency/streaming) or send edits.
- Tell us which run option you prefer (Redwood-run or EdgeFin-run).
- If Redwood-run: please share a staging API key with read/run-only scope and a preferred 2-hour window next week.

Happy to jump back on a short call if helpful.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Marissa - thanks for the recap and attachments. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Streaming measurement semantics: we need initial-token latency measured from request arrival at our edge proxy (so that includes our 10-20ms), and we care about per-chunk jitter over 95th percentile for sustained streams.

2) Staging access: we cannot provide any third party with a staging key or run in our VPC. We can run the harness internally but need the exact container image and deterministic steps to get reproducible results.

3) Workload shape: we have short chat-like prompts (avg 60 tokens input, 120 tokens output) and a small fraction (~10%) of long-form generation (400-600 tokens). I'll attach a small sample traffic_profile.json for your harness.

Can you confirm the harness will support the following knobs:
- Warmup sequences for KV cache
- Configurable batching window (ms) and max batch size
- Option to force streaming vs non-streaming runs

If you can send an explicit self-run checklist + deterministic seed settings, we'll try a run and share the logs.

Thanks,
Alice
EdgeFin - Platform / SRE
alice.gomez@edgefin.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@edgefin.com>
Cc: rafael.mendes@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-05T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO benchmark methodology

Thanks Alice - great questions. Short answers and an explicit self-run checklist below.

Measurement semantics:
- We'll measure initial-token latency from request arrival at the harness ingress by default. For Redwood-run we can also report two views: (a) harness-measured (request arrival) and (b) model-start to first token. We'll include the proxy offset so you can subtract or add as needed.

Knobs supported by the harness (all available in redwood_eval_harness_v2.zip):
- KV cache warmup: configurable warmup sequences and warmup rate.
- Batching controls: batching window (ms), max-batch-size, and per-model concurrency cap.
- Streaming toggle: run in streaming vs non-streaming mode; harness instruments per-chunk timestamps and jitter metrics.
- Deterministic seeds: harness supports seeding for sampling-based decoders and fixed-deterministic generation for reproducibility.

Self-run checklist (recommended):
1) Pull the harness: redwood_eval_harness_v2.zip and unpack.
2) Place prompt_set_edgefin_v1.jsonl in ./data/ and traffic_profile.json in ./config/.
3) Edit config/run_config.yaml: set ingress_latency_offset_ms = 15 (your proxy average); set seed = 42; set batching.window_ms = 15 and batching.max_batch_size = 64 (adjust as needed).
4) Run: ./run_benchmark.sh --config ./config/run_config.yaml --out ./results/ --mode streaming
5) Upload results: results/metrics.json and results/trace.log. Include sample_run_results.csv for quick glance.

If you prefer Redwood-run but without giving credentials, we can run the harness in our AWS account against a customer-provided public test endpoint (TLS, auth token) that you provision for the test window only. That avoids giving full staging keys.

Proposed schedule: if EdgeFin self-runs, target next Wednesday (2026-08-12) 09:00-11:00 PT; if Redwood-run, we can do Tue 2026-08-11 10:00-12:00 PT (canary + ramp). Which do you prefer?

I'll loop Rafael (runtime lead) to flag any config we'd like to include in the run.

Best,
Marissa

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-08-06T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO benchmark methodology (internal)

Marissa / Neha - quick internal note to prepare for EdgeFin's self-run:

Priority knobs to include in the results and notes section:
- Batching.window_ms: test 5 / 15 / 50 ms to show latency vs throughput tradeoffs.
- Max_batch_size: include 16 / 32 / 64.
- KV cache warmup: full-warm vs cold-start traces; include a 5-minute warmup scenario.
- Quantization profile: run at fp16 and int8-compatible quant to show cost/latency differences.
- Streaming chunk size: test 40ms vs 60ms vs 80ms pacing to capture jitter sensitivity.

We'll prepare an internal run script that populates run_config.yaml presets and a short README documenting interpretation of metrics. Also prepare a canary run plan (10% traffic for 10 minutes) in case EdgeFin wants a gradual test.

I'll attach a short note to share with the customer (we should remove any internal-only logs).

-Rafael
